title: Andrews' generating-function conjecture for linked partition ideals
statement:
A **linked partition ideal** is a set of partitions closed under the linked-partition-ideal structure introduced by Andrews. Let $G_{\mathscr{I}}(x,q)$ denote its bivariate generating function, where the coefficient of $x^m q^n$ counts partitions of $n$ with exactly $m$ parts. Let $L_1$, $L_2$, and $L_3$ be linear forms in $n_1,\ldots,n_r$, and let $Q$ be a quadratic form in these variables. **Andrews' conjecture.** Every linked partition ideal $\mathscr{I}$ has a bivariate generating function of the form

$$
G_{\mathscr{I}}(x,q)=\sum_{n_1,\ldots,n_r\ge 0}\frac{(-1)^{L_1(n_1,\ldots,n_r)}q^{Q(n_1,\ldots,n_r)+L_2(n_1,\ldots,n_r)}x^{L_3(n_1,\ldots,n_r)}}{(q^{B_1};q^{A_1})_{n_1}\cdots (q^{B_r};q^{A_r})_{n_r}}.
$$

The conjecture predicts a uniform multisum form for generating functions of linked partition ideals and is used in the paper to guide the discovery of generating-function identities. The source does not state a resolution.
source_name: Shane Chern and Zhitai Li, “Linked partition ideals and Kanade–Russell conjectures”, arXiv:1809.08655 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).
